Findings (ranked):

1. `TapticTests/DetectionStateTests.swift:23‑44` assumes a `smoothedConfidence` property is available on `DetectionState`, but `Home/DetectionState.swift:12‑102` defines no such stored/computed property or smoothing state. With the current struct the test target won’t even compile, so the detection-state regression suite is dead in the water and we can’t guard against future behavior changes. Fixing either the struct (add smoothing state/`smoothedConfidence`) or the tests to match the current API is required before the suite can run again.

2. Widget detection state is only synced inside `SharedStorage.recordTap` (`GlobalDetection/SharedStorage.swift:90‑238`). `syncToWidgetInternal` is never called when the user toggles detection on/off, nor when Siri/widgets request a state change, so `WidgetKeys.isDetecting` remains stale until the next detection event. That leaves the widget showing “off” even though detection is running (and vice versa) and makes the widget toggle unreliable. Update `toggleSoundDetection`/Siri handlers to call `SharedStorage.syncToWidget()` or otherwise write `WidgetKeys.isDetecting` whenever `soundDetectionState` changes so the widget reflects the true state immediately.

3. Alert feedback calls `AdaptiveThresholdManager.shared.recordFalsePositive`/`recordConfirmedDetection` (`GlobalDetection/SharedStorage.swift:343‑369`) and that manager exposes `adjustedThreshold(base:for:)` (`GlobalDetection/SoundDetectionConfig.swift:295‑370`), but the detection pipeline never reads those adjustments — `AppState.restartDetection` builds every `DetectionState` solely from `hapticThreshold` (`GlobalDetection/appstate.swift:370‑379`). User-submitted false-positive feedback therefore has no effect on sensitivity, defeating the advertised adaptive-threshold feature. Incorporate `AdaptiveThresholdManager` into detection-state creation (per-label thresholds) so recorded feedback actually tweaks confidence thresholds.

Next steps:
1. Sync the widget after any state toggle (appborn, Siri, widget intent) and ideally expose a single helper so both detection toggles and background handlers pick it up.
2. Decide whether `DetectionState` should keep EMA state (`smoothedConfidence`) or whether the tests should be rewritten—both the model and test suite must agree before regression coverage returns.
3. Wire the adaptive-threshold adjustments into `DetectionState` construction (probably via `AdaptiveThresholdManager.adjustedThreshold`) so feedback has measurable impact on detection sensitivity.
